DataStatistics4.correlation_coefficient:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the Pearson correlation coefficient between two equal-length numeric sequences by normalizing their covariance by the product of their standard deviations, returning 0 when the denominator is zero." correlation_coefficient]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> data1 </REF>: list[float] "First numeric sequence; must be non-empty and equal in length to data2 for a valid result"
        <REF> data2 </REF>: list[float] "Second numeric sequence; must be non-empty and equal in length to data1 for a valid result"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: float "Pearson correlation coefficient in the range [-1.0, 1.0], or 0 if the denominator is zero"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Compute n as the integer count of elements in data1 using len(data1) RESULT n]
            [COMMAND Compute mean1 as the arithmetic mean of data1: divide the sum of all elements in data1 by n RESULT mean1]
            [COMMAND Compute mean2 as the arithmetic mean of data2: divide the sum of all elements in data2 by n RESULT mean2]
            [COMMAND Compute numerator as the sum over i in range(n) of the product (data1[i] - mean1) * (data2[i] - mean2) RESULT numerator]
            [COMMAND Compute the left factor of denominator as math.sqrt of the sum over i in range(n) of (data1[i] - mean1) squared RESULT std_factor1]
            [COMMAND Compute the right factor of denominator as math.sqrt of the sum over i in range(n) of (data2[i] - mean2) squared RESULT std_factor2]
            [COMMAND Compute denominator as the product of std_factor1 and std_factor2 RESULT denominator]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the conditional return: if denominator is not equal to 0 return numerator divided by denominator, otherwise return the integer literal 0 RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: denominator equals exactly 0, meaning at least one of the two series has zero variance (all values are identical) or n is 1]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the integer literal 0 as the correlation result without performing division RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: len(data2) is greater than n: the generator expressions iterate only over indices 0 through n-1, silently ignoring extra elements in data2]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Proceed with all computations using only the first n elements of data2 and all n elements of data1, producing a result derived from mismatched data without raising an error RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: n equals 0, meaning data1 is empty, causing division by zero when computing mean1 or mean2]
        [LOG "ZeroDivisionError raised during computation of mean1 = sum(data1) / n with n == 0; no guard is present before this operation"]
        [THROW ZeroDivisionError "Raised implicitly by Python when dividing by zero during mean computation for an empty input sequence"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DataStatistics4.skewness:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the sample skewness (Fisher's adjusted third standardized moment) of a numeric dataset, returning zero when all values are identical." skewness]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> data </REF>: list[float] "Iterable of numeric values for which skewness is computed; must be non-empty and contain at least 3 elements with non-zero spread to avoid division by zero"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> skewness </REF>: float "Sample skewness of the dataset using Fisher's adjustment; returns 0.0 when standard deviation is zero"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Compute n as the integer count of elements in data using len(data) RESULT n]
            [COMMAND Compute mean as the arithmetic mean of data: sum all elements in data and divide by n RESULT mean]
            [COMMAND Compute variance as the population variance: for each element x in data sum (x - mean) squared, then divide the total by n RESULT variance]
            [COMMAND Compute std_deviation as the non-negative square root of variance using math.sqrt RESULT std_deviation]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the skewness conditional expression: if std_deviation is not equal to 0, compute the sample skewness as the sum of (x - mean) cubed for each x in data, multiplied by n, divided by the product of (n - 1), (n - 2), and std_deviation cubed; otherwise assign 0 RESULT skewness]
            [COMMAND Return skewness RESULT skewness]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: std_deviation equals 0, meaning all values in data are identical and the dataset has zero spread]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign skewness the value 0 without performing any division, short-circuiting the full skewness formula RESULT skewness]
            [COMMAND Return skewness RESULT skewness]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: data is an empty iterable, causing n to equal 0 and the division sum(data) / n to raise an exception]
        [LOG "ZeroDivisionError raised at the mean computation step because n is 0; no guard exists for empty input"]
        [THROW ZeroDivisionError "Raised when data is empty and division by n (which equals 0) is attempted during mean calculation"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: data contains fewer than 3 elements with non-zero spread, causing the denominator (n - 1) * (n - 2) to equal 0 when n is 1 or 2]
        [LOG "ZeroDivisionError raised inside the skewness conditional branch because (n - 1) * (n - 2) evaluates to 0; this path is only reached when std_deviation is not 0, so the zero-spread guard does not protect against it"]
        [THROW ZeroDivisionError "Raised when n is 1 or 2 and the dataset has non-zero spread, making the sample skewness denominator (n - 1) * (n - 2) * std_deviation^3 equal to zero"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DataStatistics4.kurtosis:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the excess kurtosis (Fisher's definition) of a numeric dataset by normalizing the fourth central moment by the fourth power of the population standard deviation and subtracting 3." kurtosis]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> data </REF>: list[numeric] "A non-empty, re-iterable sequence of numeric values for which excess kurtosis is computed; must support multiple iterations and contain at least one element to avoid ZeroDivisionError"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> kurtosis_value </REF>: float "The excess kurtosis of the input data using Fisher's definition (normal distribution yields 0); returns math.nan when all values are identical (std_dev == 0)"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Compute n as the total count of elements in data using len RESULT n]
            [COMMAND Compute mean as the arithmetic mean of data by dividing the sum of all elements by n RESULT mean]
            [COMMAND Compute std_dev as the population standard deviation: iterate data, subtract mean from each element, square the result, sum all squared differences, divide by n, then take the square root RESULT std_dev]
            [COMMAND Check whether std_dev equals exactly 0 RESULT std_dev_is_zero]
            [COMMAND Build centered_data as a new list by subtracting mean from every element in data RESULT centered_data]
            [COMMAND Compute fourth_moment as the raw fourth central moment: raise each element of centered_data to the fourth power, sum all values, then divide by n RESULT fourth_moment]
            [COMMAND Compute kurtosis_value as excess kurtosis: divide fourth_moment by std_dev raised to the fourth power, then subtract 3 RESULT kurtosis_value]
            [COMMAND Return kurtosis_value to the caller RESULT return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: std_dev equals 0, meaning all elements in data are identical and the distribution has no spread]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return math.nan immediately, bypassing all remaining computation RESULT return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: data is empty (n == 0), causing division by zero when computing mean]
        [LOG "ZeroDivisionError raised at mean = sum(data) / n because n is 0; std_dev and all subsequent steps are never reached"]
        [THROW ZeroDivisionError "Raised implicitly by Python when dividing by n where n equals 0; no explicit guard is present in the method"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: data contains non-numeric types, causing a type error during sum or element-wise subtraction]
        [LOG "TypeError raised inside sum(data) when computing mean, or inside the generator expression (x - mean) when computing std_dev or centered_data"]
        [THROW TypeError "Raised implicitly by Python when arithmetic operations are applied to incompatible types; no explicit type guard is present in the method"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
DataStatistics4.pdf:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes the Gaussian (normal) probability density function value for each element in a data list given a mean and standard deviation." pdf]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> data </REF>: list[float] "Iterable of numeric values for which the PDF is evaluated; may be empty, producing an empty result list"
        <REF> mu </REF>: float "Mean (μ) of the normal distribution; read-only scalar used in every iteration"
        <REF> sigma </REF>: float "Standard deviation (σ) of the normal distribution; must be non-zero and positive; read-only scalar used in every iteration"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> pdf_values </REF>: list[float] "List of PDF floats, one per input value in data, in the same order; empty when data is empty"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND For each element x in data, compute the normalization factor as 1 divided by (sigma multiplied by the square root of 2 * math.pi), then compute the exponent term as -0.5 multiplied by ((x minus mu) divided by sigma) squared, then multiply the normalization factor by math.exp of the exponent term to produce one float; collect all resulting floats into a new list and assign it to pdf_values RESULT pdf_values]
            [COMMAND Return pdf_values RESULT return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: data is an empty iterable]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND The list comprehension produces an empty list without error; assign the empty list to pdf_values and proceed to the return step RESULT pdf_values]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: sigma equals 0]
        [LOG "Division by zero occurs in both the normalization factor (1 / (sigma * math.sqrt(2 * math.pi))) and the standardized distance term ((x - mu) / sigma), raising ZeroDivisionError on the first iteration"]
        [THROW ZeroDivisionError "Raised by Python when sigma is zero and the comprehension attempts division; no elements are added to pdf_values before the error is raised"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

    [EXCEPTION_FLOW: Any element x in data is non-numeric]
        [LOG "The subtraction x - mu raises TypeError because the operands are incompatible types"]
        [THROW TypeError "Raised when a non-numeric value in data is encountered and cannot be subtracted from mu"]
    [END_EXCEPTION_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
